name: OpenCode
summary: An open-source AI coding agent organized as an Effect-based TypeScript workspace with durable sessions, provider/model services, tool execution, compaction, plugins, and terminal/web interfaces.
scope: session persistence, compaction, and CLI/UI surfaces

features.name: Effect service-oriented session runtime
features.description: The core package models agents, sessions, databases, buses, tools, models, and plugins as Effect services/layers; the session runner composes these services to drain input and run provider steps.
benefits: Makes runtime dependencies explicit and replaceable
Provides structured lifecycle and error composition around session execution
costs: Effect layers and service indirection increase conceptual overhead
Runtime behavior spans multiple service modules and projections

features.name: Durable session step and tool continuation loop
features.description: The session runner promotes queued or steering input, prepares context, streams provider turns, records tool calls before local effects, settles tool fibers, persists events, and continues for subsequent steps subject to agent limits.
benefits: Tool outcomes and streaming events have durable session boundaries
Continuation and step limits are explicit orchestration policies
costs: Persistence and settlement ordering add latency and failure paths
Provider, tool, database, and interruption semantics must agree

features.name: Adaptive context compaction with precomputation
features.description: Session compaction supports manual, automatic, and overflow-triggered paths, can precompute summaries as context nears a threshold, preserves a recent tail, and retries or reports typed failures.
benefits: Keeps long sessions within model context limits
Background preparation can reduce critical-path compaction work
costs: Summaries are lossy projections of history
Thresholds, retries, model limits, and failure states complicate reproducibility

features.name: Reloadable plugin and agent configuration boundary
features.description: OpenCode maintains plugin activation scopes and failures, publishes plugin updates, and provides configurable agent definitions with selectable primary and subagent modes.
benefits: Extends providers, tools, commands, and behavior without changing the core runtime
Activation scopes allow cleanup and revision-aware reloads
costs: Plugin lifecycle and failure recovery add state transitions
Dynamic configuration can change available tools and prompts during a long-lived process

mathematical_views.question: How do session, model, database, tool, plugin, and event services compose into a runnable coding-agent location?
assumptions: Services are vertices and layer requirements are directed edges
Effect scopes represent resource lifetime boundaries
The view abstracts the full dynamic call graph and scheduler
A valid layer composition does not prove application-level correctness

mathematical_views.question: Which input, compaction, provider, tool, retry, and continuation events advance or settle a session step?
assumptions: A session has an ordered durable history and input inbox
A provider turn and local tool settlement form one step transition
Interruptions and typed failures are explicit terminal or retry transitions
The model abstracts SQLite schema and provider semantics

mathematical_views.model: Lossy context projection with threshold policy
mathematical_views.question: When does a session replace history with a summary and retained tail, and what state is preserved?
assumptions: Compaction maps a history prefix to a summary plus selected recent messages
Threshold and overflow triggers are policy predicates over token estimates
Background summaries may become stale before being swapped in
The projection is explanatory and does not establish semantic equivalence

costs: More indirection for tracing a request

benefits: Recoverable tool and provider event boundary
costs: Durability and concurrency increase operational complexity
History is summarized under evolving heuristics
Plugin revisions and failures require lifecycle coordination
